messages:
Maya (Support): Customer FinHealth reports that their Trace View shows 0 spans for a set of successful API requests since ~09:10 UTC. They provided request IDs and screenshots of the empty trace panel. Customer is seeing errors in dashboard alerts (span count = 0) but app logs show 200s. Asking for urgent help, customer is on a paid SLA. :red_circle:

Ethan (Eng): Can you paste one of the request IDs and any sample payload/headers? Also which clusters/tenant is this for? Could be a tag/field mismatch in the trace join.

Maya (Support): Sample IDs: req-9a3f2b1e, req-9a3f2b2a, req-9a3f2b5f. Tenant: finhealth-prod-us. Screenshot: https://redwood.corp/attachments/finhealth-empty-trace.png. Logs show header `x-rid: req-9a3f2b1e` and `trace-id: 4b7f2c9a`.

Priya (Infra): Noted. There was a small indexer schema tweak in the last deploy at 09:05 UTC. Deploy-bot said: 

deploy-bot: new deployment to indexer-service v2.14.1 by priya -- changelog: mapping for `request.headers` normalization.

Ethan (Eng): That could explain it — if the normalizer renamed `request.headers.x-request-id` -> `request.request_id` then the trace linking query might miss `x-rid`. Can you show the raw event ingest for one of the request IDs (the event that should produce spans)?

Maya (Support): Pasted raw event snippet from customer's ingest pipeline: 
```
{ "ts": "2026-03-17T09:08:43Z", "tenant": "finhealth-prod-us", "request": { "method": "POST", "path": "/v1/pay", "headers": { "x-rid": "req-9a3f2b1e", "trace-id": "4b7f2c9a" } }, "spans": [ {"name": "auth.lookup", "duration_ms": 12 } ] }
```

Ethan (Eng): OK that payload still has x-rid. Two hypotheses: 1) indexer mapping change dropped the `request.headers` subtree for certain tenants, 2) trace join job uses `request.request_id` not `request.headers.x-rid` after the deploy. I'll grep the release and routing rules.

Priya (Infra): I'm seeing a spike in consumer lag for the indexer input topic around 09:06. Dashboard: https://observability/redwood/indexer/consumer-lag?env=prod&tenant=finhealth-prod-us — lag peaked ~3.2k messages and is currently ~800. That would cause delayed spans and possible partial writes.

Liam (SRE): Can you run a quick query to check whether trace documents were indexed but with a different field name? Try in ES: 
```
GET /traces/_search?q=tenant:finhealth-prod-us AND request.request_id:req-9a3f2b1e
```
then 
```
GET /traces/_search?q=tenant:finhealth-prod-us AND request.headers.x-rid:req-9a3f2b1e
```

Ethan (Eng): I ran a broader lookup on a dev snapshot and found a few traces indexed under `request.request_id` for other tenants after the same deploy. So mapping drift is real. The join layer for the Trace View expects `request.headers.x-rid` — mismatch explains empty UI.

Maya (Support): Quick customer update: told them we're investigating and asked for patience. They asked for ETA and if data will be lost.

Priya (Infra): Short-term mitigation: re-run indexer with backward-compatible mapping and reindex the affected time window for finhealth-prod-us. Long-term: add a schema-checker gate in deploy pipeline. I can start the reindex job for that tenant for 08:50–09:20 UTC. Command I will run: 
```
infractl reindex --tenant finhealth-prod-us --start 2026-03-17T08:50:00Z --end 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z --mapping-override legacy
```
ETA ~25–40m depending on backfill speed.

Ethan (Eng): Will also prepare a quick patch to make the trace join accept either `request.request_id` or `request.headers.x-rid` to avoid user-facing gaps during the roll. Can we do a small canary for one tenant first?

Liam (SRE): Please schedule the canary on a low-traffic tenant first. Keep oncall looped for rollback steps. Also confirm whether billing/usage metrics are affected — if span counts retroactively change it may impact alerting.

Maya (Support): Opening internal incident INC-9721, escalated to SRE + Infra + Eng. Notified account manager and CS lead, customer-facing ETA: 40m for reindex, will follow-up in 30m with progress. :phone:

Priya (Infra): Starting backfill now, job id backfill-7893. Progress will post to job channel. Will also tag this deploy for rollback if mappings show additional drift.

Maya (Support): Thanks everyone — I'll update the customer and paste the INC in the support ticket. If anyone finds more affected tenants please add to INC-9721. :thumbsup:
